scope: Humidity-growth quantitative table (plan Step 5): f(RH) growth factors of the OPAC-pinned component classes, extracted from the pinned 1998 component data files recovered in this survey. Purpose is the magnitude comparison against the cross-event inversion pool ratio R=7.110 ONLY - this table makes no claim about whether the humidity axis explains any event, and no conclusion is drawn.

method.extraction: ext.coef at wavelength 0.550 um read from each pinned OPAC component file's optical table (the files' extinction is normalized ext.nor=1 at 0.55 um and is expressed per 1 particle/cm3). Growth factor g(RH) = ext550(RH)/ext550(RH=0%). At fixed number density N and fixed layer geometry, column AOD550 scales linearly with ext550(RH), so g(RH) is also the AOD growth factor per component at fixed N.
method.conversion_notes: OPAC aerosol types (as used by the pinned prior_parameters contract) are mixtures of components; type-level humidity growth depends on the mixture composition and is NOT computed here. The low-layer increment of the production model is a 0-10 km layer; applying g(RH) as an AOD multiplier assumes the layer's number density profile is held fixed while particle wet size changes - the OPAC files' own construction (same dry size distribution, RH-dependent wet radius).
method.inputs: validation/results/prior_source_survey/sources.json entry opac1998_component_data_files (26 pinned files, sha256 per file); version identification (original 1998 dataset) recorded there.

pool_comparison_anchor.comparison_statement: Magnitude comparison only: the full-humidity-axis growth (dry -> 99% RH) spans x12.1-x18.6 depending on component; the 50% -> 99% span is x7.4-x7.6 (WASO/SSAM, the two components with the 50% and 99% files both pinned), the same order as R=7.110; the moderate spans are much smaller (50% -> 80%: x1.49-x1.52 for SSAM/SSCM; 50% -> 90%: x2.07-x2.17; 70% -> 98%: x3.92-x4.04). Whether an ambient-RH difference between eclipse events could span the pool is not assessed here; the table only states which RH spans produce which growth factors.
